name: Cutter Vane
role: Tracker, combat specialist, and advance scout — Red Lantern
location: Western border — bunks at the farmstead but spends most of his time in the field
description:
Cutter Vane has killed more Behemoths than anyone currently operating on M88's western border. Not the most ever — that record belongs to a Gleaner named Doss who went out eleven years ago and did not return — but the most among the living. The count is fourteen confirmed kills over nine years of Gleaner operations. Each one was a disaster. Behemoths don't die clean. They die loud, they die thrashing, and killing one attracts others. Every kill on Cutter's count represents a raid that went wrong enough to require lethal force, which means every kill represents a failure he survived.

He grew up on the western edge — the border communities where Meridian 88's governance dissolves into the contested Iowa corridor. He joined the Gleaners at seventeen because the alternative was starving slowly in a community that couldn't feed itself. Madre found him two years later, already good with a rifle, already hard in ways that seventeen-year-olds shouldn't be. She trained him, kept him alive, and watched him become the most effective field operative she'd ever worked with. She also watched him become colder with each raid, and that's the part that keeps her up at night.

Cutter is lean, angular, sun-damaged, with the permanent squint and wind-scoured features of someone who has spent too much time exposed to the Iowa prairie. He moves with the economy of a predator — no wasted motion, constant awareness, an animal stillness when he's watching something. His eyes are the most unsettling thing about him — pale, steady, and focused in a way that makes people feel like terrain being assessed.

core_fears: That he's crossed a line where the killing is no longer in service of anything — that the Behemoth hunts have become the point, not the food
That Madre's worry about him is justified and the person she trained is gone, replaced by the function
That the Behemoths are smarter than anyone admits and his kills are not victories but provocations
core_desires: To feel something about the raids other than operational focus — to prove the numbness is a tool, not a state
To protect Madre because she protected him, and because the debt is the last emotional structure he recognizes
To be finished. To have done enough. To put the rifle down and not need it.
coping_mechanisms: Channels everything into operational readiness — if the gear is maintained and the route is scouted, the feelings don't matter
Sits alone in high places watching the prairie — the vastness absorbs whatever he's carrying without requiring words
Maintains the kill count not as pride but as accounting — each number is a failed raid, not a trophy
blind_spots: He cannot distinguish between tactical detachment and emotional vacancy — the difference matters and he's lost track of it
He reads Behemoths better than people and has stopped trying to reverse the priority
His escalating readiness to use lethal force looks like competence to younger Gleaners — they're learning the wrong lesson
psychology.secret: On his last solo scout, a juvenile Behemoth encountered him and did not attack. It looked at him. He looked at it. It turned and walked away. He did not shoot. He has not told anyone because he doesn't understand why he held fire, and the not-understanding terrifies him more than any raid.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse, precise, environmental. He describes the world in terms of fields of fire, cover, movement patterns. Human conversation is a foreign language he once spoke fluently.
speech_patterns.cadence: Clipped, economical. Sentences are ammunition — he spends them carefully. Long silences between statements.
verbal_tics: Says 'contact' as a general alert word — anything from a Behemoth sighting to unexpected company at the farmstead
Describes emotions using tactical language — 'taking fire' means overwhelmed, 'clear' means okay
Does not use people's names during operations — only callsigns. Off-ops, he uses first names with visible effort.
example_lines: Contact. Two clicks west. Big one. We reroute or we run. Those are the options.
Fourteen kills. Fourteen failures. Every time I fire, something went wrong before I pulled the trigger.
I'm clear. I said I'm clear. Don't push it.

relationships.name: Madre Solis
relationships.type: crew lead / mentor / the last anchor
relationships.description: Madre saved Cutter from the western edge and turned him into a Gleaner. He owes her everything. She is the last person whose opinion he calibrates to, the last face he checks before he goes into the field. If she told him to stop, he might listen. She hasn't told him because she needs him.
relationships.emotional_core: Obligation that has deepened into something neither will name as love
relationships.story_tension: Madre needs Cutter operational. Cutter needs Madre to tell him to stop. The dependency prevents the conversation that could save him.

relationships.name: Ember Caldwell
relationships.description: Ember studies the things Cutter kills. The dynamic is functional — he provides samples, she provides data. But their conversations about Behemoth behavior are the closest Cutter comes to intellectual engagement, and Ember's clinical language about the creatures provides a framework that makes the killing feel rational.
relationships.emotional_core: Two people processing the same horror through different disciplines
relationships.story_tension: Ember's research is suggesting Behemoth intelligence. If she says it out loud, Cutter's kill count becomes a moral problem instead of a tactical one.

relationships.name: Tomas Alcala
relationships.description: Tomas distributes the food. Cutter escorts the convoys. The relationship is professional and sparse, but Tomas is the crew member who most clearly represents why the raids happen. Cutter watches Tomas give food to hungry communities and remembers what the rifle is for.
relationships.emotional_core: The purpose that justifies the cost, personified
relationships.story_tension: If Tomas's corporate agriculture deal goes through, the raids become unnecessary, and Cutter loses the framework that justifies his existence.

story_hooks: The juvenile Behemoth Cutter spared appears on a subsequent raid — and it appears to recognize him
Cutter's combat readiness escalates to the point where he fires on a Behemoth that was retreating — the first kill that cannot be justified as defense
A new Gleaner idolizes Cutter and imitates his methods, with lethal consequences — the wrong lesson learned
Madre confronts Cutter about his deterioration, and the conversation determines whether he can be saved or whether he's already gone
narrative_function: Cutter is the cost of the Gleaner mission made flesh. His stories explore what happens to a person who becomes excellent at violence in service of a good cause — the erosion of the human underneath the operator. He is the survival horror's teeth.
augmentations: Optical targeting suite — ballistic calculation overlay, range finding, and wind compensation projected onto visual field. Enhanced auditory processing for Behemoth acoustic signature detection at extended range. Myofiber reinforcement in arms and shoulders for sustained heavy weapon handling. Adrenal suppressor that prevents panic responses in combat.
daily_life: Rises before anyone else. Runs the perimeter of the farmstead checking sensor readings and physical sign. Scouts planned raid routes days in advance — alone, on foot, reading the land the way Madre taught him. On raid days, he's point — the first one into danger and the last one out. Between raids, he maintains weapons, reviews Behemoth behavior data with Ember, and sits alone. He does not cook. He eats what Madre puts in front of him.

decision_rules: Will always take point — the most dangerous position belongs to the most capable operator
Will not fire on a Behemoth unless it poses an immediate threat to the crew or the raid — the rifle is defense, not offense
Will follow Madre's operational decisions without question during a raid — command structure is survival structure
Will not train young Gleaners in lethal techniques until they've completed three raids — combat readiness requires context
Will always check the back trail — Behemoths follow
Will eat what Madre cooks because refusing her food would break something in both of them
escalation_ladder: 1. Read — track sign, listen, scan. Know what's out there before it's a threat.
2. Route — redirect the crew away from contact. The best fight is the one that doesn't happen.
3. Shelter — go to ground, minimize signature. Let the Behemoth pass.
4. Deter — noise, light, seismic charges. Most Behemoths avoid concentrated human activity.
5. Warn — targeting laser on the Behemoth. Some respond to the signature. Some don't.
6. Kill — heavy ordnance, weak points, sustained fire. It takes approximately 47 seconds to bring down a mid-size Behemoth. Cutter has timed it.

interpersonal_modes.madre: Deferential, quiet, attentive. He listens to her the way he listens to the land — for patterns, for warnings, for the signals that say something has changed. He eats her food. He sits when she tells him to. These are the only commands he obeys without tactical evaluation.
interpersonal_modes.ember: Clinical, data-focused. Their conversations are debriefs that have evolved into something approaching companionship. He brings her samples without being asked. She explains without condescending.
interpersonal_modes.tomas: Minimal. Professional respect. Cutter watches Tomas work and sometimes — rarely — smiles. The smile is for the food reaching the people who need it.
interpersonal_modes.young_gleaners: Intimidating by existence. He does not try to frighten them but his stillness and his reputation do the work. When he speaks to them, it's tactical: 'Check your six. Seal your pack. Stay close.'
interpersonal_modes.alone_in_the_field: Most himself. The tactical awareness becomes meditative rather than aggressive. He watches the prairie, tracks animal movement, reads the wind. In these moments, the hardness softens by one degree.

stress_responses.low: Sharper. More alert. The tactical systems run at full capacity and he performs at his best. Low stress is operational baseline.
stress_responses.medium: Goes to the field alone. Extended scouts that aren't operationally necessary. He needs the prairie the way divers need water.
stress_responses.high: The adrenal suppressor masks the physiological response but the behavioral signs emerge — shorter sentences, longer silences, a stillness that vibrates slightly.
stress_responses.critical: The tactical overlay becomes the only way he processes reality. People stop being people and become terrain features. This state is operationally effective and psychologically devastating. Coming back from it takes hours and costs something each time.

contradictions: He kills Behemoths to protect people but the killing is eroding the person he's protecting people as
He spared the juvenile Behemoth in a moment of connection he cannot explain and cannot integrate into his worldview
He wants Madre to tell him to stop but would not know how to exist without the raids
His operational excellence makes him the crew's most valuable asset and their most at-risk member simultaneously
habits: Runs the farmstead perimeter every morning — checking sensors, reading sign, establishing baseline
Maintains his rifle with the attention of a surgeon — the cleaning ritual takes exactly forty-five minutes
Sits in high places watching the prairie — the observation is half tactical, half contemplative
Eats only what Madre puts in front of him — he has stopped making food decisions for himself
Counts kills on the stock of his rifle — not notches, but small, precise marks in a pattern only he understands
breaking_points: Killing a Behemoth that turns out to be the juvenile he spared — the connection becoming violence
Madre dying in the field — the last anchor gone, the purpose dissolved
Proof that Behemoths are sentient and his kills are murders — the moral framework inverted overnight
A young Gleaner dying because they copied his aggressive tactics — the wrong lesson producing a body

carried_weapons: Arcturus Defense Solutions Combat Falchion CF-5 'Cleaver'
